examples.en: The company promotes its new product on TV.
They loudly advertised the sale in front of the shop.
There are many ads that promote the good points.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 맛집을 친구들에게 선전하고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm promoting my neighborhood's good restaurant to my friends.
You must not advertise in a way that differs from the facts.
We're looking for a model to promote the new product.

explain: 선전하다는 어떤 물건이나 생각을 사람들이 알도록 널리 알리는 거예요. '광고하다'는 주로 상품을 팔려고 알리는 일이고, 선전하다는 정치나 사상을 알릴 때도 써서 범위가 더 넓어요. 일상에서는 '광고하다'를 더 자주 들을 수 있어요.

phrases.en: They advertise the new shop on the internet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '선전하다'보다 더 자주 쓰는 비슷한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word that is used more often than 선전하다 in daily life.

phrases.en: We promoted our school's event widely.
phrases.nuance_ko: '널리'를 붙이면 많은 사람에게 알린다는 느낌이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 널리 stresses telling many people.

phrases.example: 그 회사는 새 노래를 열심히 선전하고 있어요.
phrases.en: That company is eagerly promoting the new song.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 계속 알리는 중이라는 것을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say the promotion is happening now.

explain_en: 선전하다 is to spread the word about something so people know it. '광고하다' is mainly promoting products to sell them, while 선전하다 also covers politics and ideas, so its range is wider. In daily talk you hear '광고하다' more often.

examples.en: I was quite surprised to hear the news.
This incident was emotionally quite hard on me.
It cost a good deal more than I expected.

examples.ko: 처음 만난 사람들 앞에서 적잖이 긴장했어요.
examples.en: I got pretty nervous in front of people I'd just met.

examples.ko: 아이가 갑자기 울어서 부모님이 적잖이 당황하셨어요.
examples.en: The child suddenly cried, and the parents were quite flustered.

examples.ko: 그 일은 우리 팀에 적잖이 도움이 됐어요.
examples.en: That work helped our team quite a lot.

explain: '적지 않게'라는 뜻이지만 '많이'보다 말하는 사람이 정도를 눈여겨본다는 느낌이 있어요. '놀라다', '당황하다', '실망하다' 같은 감정을 나타내는 말과 특히 자주 써요. 말할 때는 '꽤'나 '많이'를 더 자주 쓰고, '적잖이'는 글이나 조금 격식 있는 말에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 이번 일은 적지 않게 걱정이 됐어요.
phrases.en: I was quite worried about this matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: '적잖이'를 풀어 쓴 말로, 조금 더 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The spelled-out form of 적잖이, a bit more casual.

phrases.en: I was quite flustered when asked a sudden question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정을 나타내는 동사와 자주 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs often with verbs of emotion.

phrases.en: A good number of people came to the event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸미는 형태로, '적지 않은'과 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: Modifier form before a noun, same as 적지 않은.

explain_en: It means 'not a little', and it sounds like the speaker is noting how big the degree is. It is especially common with emotion verbs such as 놀라다, 당황하다 and 실망하다. In speech people use '꽤' or '많이' more often, while '적잖이' shows up more in writing and slightly formal speech.

t90.ax: That work helped our team quite a lot.

en: to handle; to treat; to deal in

examples.en: This shop carries imported snacks.
Please don't treat me like a child.

examples.ko: 깨지기 쉬운 물건이니까 조심해서 취급해 주세요.
examples.en: It breaks easily, so please handle it with care.
They treated it as a special case.
Our company deals in used cars.
It's a place that treats every customer the same.

explain: 가게가 어떤 물건을 파는지 말할 때는 '취급하다'가 '팔다'보다 직업적이고 자연스러워요. 사람을 '~처럼 취급하다'로 대하는 태도를 말할 때는 대부분 기분이 나쁜 상황이에요. 물건을 다룰 때는 '취급 주의'라는 표시를 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: Sorry, but we don't carry that product.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게에서 그 물건을 팔지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used by a shop to say it doesn't sell a certain item.

phrases.en: This box says handle with care.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 조심해서 다루라는 표시에 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A set phrase on labels telling people to handle something carefully.

phrases.en: Please don't treat your younger sibling like a baby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 어떤 존재로 보고 대한다는 뜻이고, 보통 불만스러운 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means treating someone as if they were something, usually in a frustrating situation.

explain_en: A shop sells goods, or you treat someone as something. For what a shop sells, 취급하다 sounds more professional than 팔다. '~처럼 취급하다' is about how someone is treated and is mostly used when you feel disrespected. On parcels you often see the label '취급 주의' (handle with care).

dis.h: handle goods, or regard someone as something
gh: treat a person well or in a certain way

p.n: 취급하다 is how you regard them; 대우하다 is how you act toward them.

t90.ax: Our company deals in used cars.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 운동장에서 닭싸움을 자주 했어요.
examples.en: As a kid, I often played chicken fight on the playground.

examples.ko: 닭싸움에서 진 사람이 간식을 사기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided that whoever loses the chicken fight buys the snacks.
I wanted to play chicken fight, so I called my friends.
I sprained my ankle while playing chicken fight.
Do kids these days know chicken fight too?
In chicken fight, a light kid has the advantage.

explain: 실제 닭끼리의 싸움을 뜻하기도 하지만, 말할 때는 한 발로 서서 서로 밀치는 아이들 놀이를 가리킬 때가 많아요. 문맥을 보면 어느 쪽인지 알 수 있어요.

phrases.en: I played chicken fight with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이들 놀이를 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing for the children's game.

phrases.en: I won the chicken fight and felt good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이의 승패를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about winning or losing the game.

phrases.en: We play the chicken fight game on the playground.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀이라는 뜻을 분명히 해서 실제 닭싸움과 구분해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Makes clear it is the game, not real cockfighting.

explain_en: It can mean a fight between actual chickens, but in conversation it often refers to the children's game where you stand on one leg and push each other. The context tells you which one is meant.

examples.en: I went to a billiard hall with friends and played a game.
A new billiard hall opened in my neighborhood.
How much is the billiard hall per hour?

examples.ko: 대학교 앞 당구장은 늘 학생들로 붐벼요.
examples.en: The billiard hall in front of the university is always crowded with students.
My father worked at a billiard hall when he was young.
It rained, so I spent time at the billiard hall.

explain: '당구장'은 당구를 칠 수 있는 가게예요. 한국에서는 '당구를 치다'라고 하고, '당구를 하다'도 써요. 같은 방식으로 '볼링장', '탁구장'이라고 하는 곳이 있어요.

phrases.en: I meet my friends at the billiard hall every weekend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사 '에서'를 붙여 그곳에서 하는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With the particle 에서 to say what you do there.

phrases.en: I sometimes play billiards with my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 당구장에서 하는 일을 말할 때 '당구를 치다'가 가장 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: '당구를 치다' is the most natural way to say what you do at a billiard hall.

phrases.en: The neighborhood billiard hall stays open late at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집 근처의 가까운 당구장을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a billiard hall near your home.

explain_en: '당구장' is a shop where you can play billiards. The verb is '치다' as in '당구를 치다', and '당구를 하다' also works. The same '-장' pattern gives '볼링장' and '탁구장'.

examples.en: Go stones come in black and white.
The child lined up the go stones in a row.
I'm upset because I lost one go stone.
We played five-in-a-row with go stones.
The go stones spilled onto the floor.
The sound of a go stone clicked sharply.

explain: 바둑을 둘 때 판 위에 놓는 검은 돌과 흰 돌을 말해요. '바둑알'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 돌을 놓을 때는 '바둑돌을 놓다/두다'라고 말해요.

phrases.en: I put the go stones in the container and tidied up.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바둑돌'과 같은 뜻이에요. 둘 다 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '바둑돌'; both sound natural.

phrases.en: Grandfather placed the go stone carefully.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바둑 둘 때 돌을 판 위에 놓는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes placing a stone on the board during a game.

phrases.en: There are more white go stones left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색을 붙여 검은 돌과 흰 돌을 구분해서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a color to tell the black and white stones apart.

explain_en: It refers to the black and white stones placed on the board in go. '바둑알' is used with the same meaning. When placing a stone, you say '바둑돌을 놓다/두다'.

examples.en: We played the triangle in music class.
The triangle's sound rings out clear and long.
Although small, the triangle is an important instrument in an orchestra.
The child kept the beat with a triangle.

examples.ko: 공연에서 트라이앵글이 한 번 울리자 모두 조용해졌어요.
examples.en: When the triangle rang once in the performance, everyone fell quiet.

examples.ko: 어린이 합주에서 제 아들이 트라이앵글을 맡았어요.
examples.en: In the children's ensemble, my son took the triangle.

explain: 악기 이름이라 '트라이앵글을 치다'처럼 '치다'와 같이 써요. 악기마다 동사가 달라서 피아노와 기타는 '치다', 바이올린은 '켜다'처럼 함께 외워 두세요. 도형은 '삼각형'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 트라이앵글 연주는 쉬워 보여도 박자가 중요해요.
phrases.en: Playing the triangle looks easy, but rhythm is important.
phrases.nuance_ko: 악기를 연주하는 일 전체를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the act of playing the instrument.

phrases.en: The teacher rang the triangle and the class began.
phrases.nuance_ko: 소리를 내서 신호를 줄 때는 '울리다'도 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: '울리다' is also natural when sounding it as a signal.

phrases.en: We played the triangle and the tambourine together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 음악 시간에 함께 쓰는 작은 악기와 같이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Mentioned with other small instruments used in music class.

explain_en: Loanword: only the music instrument, heard in music class and orchestras. It is the name of an instrument, used as '트라이앵글을 치다'. The verb differs by instrument: '치다' for piano and guitar, '켜다' for violin, so learn them together. The shape is called '삼각형'.

t90.ax: We played the triangle in music class.

examples.en: I sweated heavily in the steam room.
The weather today is hot like a sauna.

examples.ko: 찜질방 한증막에는 너무 오래 있지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't stay too long in the sauna room at the jjimjilbang.

examples.ko: 한증막에 들어가면 숨이 막힐 것 같아요.
examples.en: When I go into the steam room, I feel like I can't breathe.
We decided to go to the sauna with family on the weekend.
I ate boiled eggs inside the sauna room.

explain: 찜질방 등에서 아주 뜨겁게 데운 방을 말해요. 날씨가 몹시 더울 때 '한증막 같다'는 비유로도 자주 써요. 비슷한 말로 '사우나'가 있지만 한증막은 한국식 뜨거운 방 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.example: 에어컨이 고장 나서 교실이 한증막 같아요.
phrases.en: to be like a steam room
phrases.nuance_ko: 실내나 날씨가 숨 막힐 만큼 몹시 덥다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for a room or weather that is stiflingly hot.

explain_en: It refers to a very hot room, such as in a jjimjilbang. People also use it as a figure of speech, '한증막 같다', when the weather is extremely hot. '사우나' is a similar word, but 한증막 feels more like a Korean-style hot room.

en: to fold; to fold up; to fold neatly

examples.en: I fold the dry laundry on the bed.

examples.ko: 아침에 일어나서 이불을 개켜서 장롱에 넣었어요.
examples.en: I got up in the morning, folded the blanket and put it in the wardrobe.

examples.ko: 옷을 개킬 때 소매를 먼저 접어요.
examples.en: When I fold clothes, I fold the sleeves first.

examples.ko: 엄마가 개켜 놓은 수건이 선반에 있어요.
examples.en: The towels Mom folded are on the shelf.
I told my younger sibling to fold the laundry.

examples.ko: 옷을 개키면 서랍에 더 많이 들어가요.
examples.en: If you fold clothes, more of them fit in the drawer.

explain: 빨래나 이불을 접어서 차곡차곡 포개 두는 일에 써요. '이불을 개다'라고도 하는데, '개다'는 날씨가 맑아질 때도 쓰니까 문맥으로 구별해요. 종이나 우산을 접는 것은 보통 '접다'를 써요.

phrases.en: I fold the washed clothes and put them in the drawer.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빨래를 차곡차곡 접어 정리할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most common when neatly folding laundry.

phrases.en: I folded the blanket and left it.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 놓다'를 붙여 접어서 그대로 둔 상태를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 놓다' shows the folded state is left as it is.

phrases.en: I fold my blanket every morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '개키다'를 줄인 말이에요. 날씨가 '개다'와는 문맥으로 구별해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of '개키다'. Tell it apart from the weather '개다' by context.

explain_en: It is used for folding laundry or bedding and stacking it neatly. You can also say '이불을 개다', but '개다' also means the weather clearing up, so rely on context. For folding paper or an umbrella people usually use '접다'.

t90.ax: I fold the dry laundry on the bed.

en: to be visible from inside; to be seen in the distance

examples.en: You can see the sea from my window.
The garden was clearly visible through the living room window.
This room is high up, so you can see far out.

examples.ko: 커튼을 열면 시장 골목이 내다보이는 집이에요.
examples.en: It's a house where you can see the market alley when you open the curtain.

examples.ko: 안개 때문에 밖이 잘 내다보이지 않아요.
examples.en: Because of the fog, I can't see outside well.

examples.ko: 옥상에 올라가면 동네가 다 내다보일 거예요.
examples.en: If you go up to the rooftop, you'll be able to see the whole neighborhood.

explain: 그냥 '보이다'와 달리 창문이나 문처럼 안쪽에서 바깥이 눈에 들어올 때 써요. 장소가 주어가 되어서 '이 방에서는 바다가 내다보여요'처럼 말해요. 보는 사람이 주어이면 '내다보다'를 써요.

phrases.en: You can see the mountain from this room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 표제어의 해요체 현재형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form of the headword.

phrases.example: 안개가 껴서 밖이 잘 내다보이지 않아요.
phrases.en: It's foggy, so I can't see outside well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 바깥이 잘 안 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says the outside is hard to see.

phrases.en: When I lie on the bed, I can see out the window.
phrases.nuance_ko: '창밖이'를 앞에 붙여 창문 밖의 풍경이 보인다고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '창밖이' it means the scenery outside the window is visible.
phrases.en_equiv: the view outside the window is visible

explain_en: Unlike plain '보이다', it is used when the outside comes into view from the inside, such as through a window or door. A place often serves as the subject, as in '이 방에서는 바다가 내다보여요'. When the person is the subject, use '내다보다'.

en: to be shabby; to be unsightly; to be tacky

examples.ko: 방이 너무 너절해서 손님을 못 불러요.
examples.en: My room is so shabby that I can't invite guests.

examples.ko: 너절한 옷차림으로 면접에 가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't go to an interview in shabby clothes.

examples.ko: 책상 위가 너절해 보이니까 좀 치우세요.
examples.en: Your desk looks messy, so please tidy it up.
Stop making cheap excuses.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 겉은 멀쩡한데 안은 너절해요.
examples.en: That shop looks fine outside but is shabby inside.
It is a storage room full of nothing but junk.

explain: '지저분하다'가 더러운 느낌이라면 '너절하다'는 허름하고 질이 낮아 보이는 느낌이 강해요. 물건이나 옷차림뿐 아니라 말이나 행동이 치사할 때도 써요. 비슷한 '너저분하다'는 물건이 어지럽게 널린 모습에 더 가까워요.

phrases.en: The clothes are worn out, so they look a bit shabby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 허름하다는 인상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the impression that something looks shabby on the outside.

phrases.example: 그는 늦게 와 놓고 너절한 변명만 늘어놓았어요.
phrases.en: He came late and then just kept making lame excuses.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말이나 행동이 치사하고 질이 낮을 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for words or actions that are petty and low in quality.

phrases.en: The house is small, but it isn't shabby.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 깔끔하다는 뜻을 간접적으로 전해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form indirectly says that it is neat.

explain_en: '지저분하다' means dirty or messy, while '너절하다' stresses a cheap, low-quality look. It can describe things and clothes, and also petty words or behavior. The similar '너저분하다' is closer to things lying around in disorder.

en: to be spacious; to be roomy

examples.ko: 이 방은 널찍해서 가구를 놓기 좋아요.
examples.en: This room is spacious, so it's good for placing furniture.
It's convenient because there's a roomy parking lot.
The living room feels spacious.

examples.ko: 우리 좀 더 널찍한 집으로 이사 가요.
examples.en: Let's move to a somewhat roomier house.
Studying is more comfortable when the desk is roomy.
This cafe isn't spacious, but it's cozy.

explain: 그냥 '넓다'보다 공간에 여유가 있고 시원하다는 좋은 느낌이 있어요. 방, 마당, 자리처럼 공간을 말할 때 잘 써요.

phrases.en: We moved into a spacious room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 활용형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun.

phrases.en: The new office is roomy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 현재 상태를 말하는 해요체 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite present-tense form.

phrases.en: I want to use the desk with plenty of space.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-게'를 붙이면 공간을 여유 있게 쓴다는 뜻이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-게', it means using space generously.

explain_en: Compared to plain '넓다', it carries a pleasant feeling of room to spare and openness. It fits spaces such as rooms, yards and seats.

en: to be piping hot; to be steaming hot

examples.en: In cold winter, a piping hot broth is the best.
The floor is nice and hot, so it's comfortable to sit here.
I turned on the boiler and the room warmed up nice and hot.
I lay down on the steaming hot floor at the sauna.
The sweet potato I just baked is still piping hot.

examples.ko: 오늘 목욕탕 물이 너무 뜨끈뜨끈하지 않아요?
examples.en: Isn't the bathhouse water too hot today?

explain: '따뜻하다'보다 훨씬 뜨겁고, 몸이 풀릴 만큼 열기가 느껴질 때 써요. 온돌 바닥, 국물, 목욕물처럼 몸을 녹여 주는 것에 잘 어울려요. '뜨끈하다'로 줄여서 말하기도 해요.

phrases.en: Drinking hot soup loosens my body up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸을 녹여 주는 뜨거운 국물에 가장 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits best with hot soup that warms you up.

phrases.en: The floor is nice and hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 상태를 해요체로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite form for describing how things are now.

phrases.en: The bath water is nice and hot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뜨끈뜨끈하다'를 줄인 말로, 더 짧고 편하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened, more casual form of the word.

explain_en: Stronger, deeper heat, like hot soup or a heated room (뜨끈뜨끈한 국밥) It describes something much hotter than '따뜻하다', hot enough to relax your body. It suits heated floors, soup and bath water that warm you up. People also shorten it to '뜨끈하다'.

t90.ax: Isn't the bathhouse water too hot today?

examples.ko: 바늘귀가 너무 작아서 실이 안 들어가요.
examples.en: The eye of the needle is so small that the thread won't go in.

examples.ko: 눈이 나빠서 바늘귀에 실을 꿰기 힘들어요.
examples.en: My eyesight is bad, so it's hard to thread the needle.
Please switch to a needle with a bigger eye.

examples.ko: 할머니가 바늘귀에 실을 꿰 달라고 부탁하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother asked me to thread the needle for her.
The thread keeps slipping out of the needle's eye.
I couldn't find the needle's eye, so I turned on the light.

explain: 몸의 귀가 아니라 바늘에서 실을 꿰는 작은 구멍을 말해요. '바늘귀에 실을 꿰다'처럼 '꿰다'와 함께 자주 써요.

phrases.example: 바늘귀에 실을 꿰는 일이 쉽지 않아요.
phrases.en: Threading a needle isn't easy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바늘귀와 가장 자주 함께 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase paired with 바늘귀.

phrases.example: 바늘귀가 작아서 굵은 실은 안 들어가요.
phrases.en: The eye of the needle is small, so thick thread won't go through.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '작다, 크다'와 함께 바늘의 크기를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with adjectives like '작다' or '크다' to describe the needle's size.

phrases.en: It's dark, so I can't see the eye of the needle well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이 나쁘거나 어두울 때 실 꿰기 힘든 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the trouble of threading when eyesight is poor or the light is dim.

explain_en: The hole in a needle for thread (저는 눈이 나빠서 바늘귀에 실을 끼우기 힘들어요.) This is not the ear on your body; it is the small hole in a needle where the thread goes. It is often used with '꿰다', as in '바늘귀에 실을 꿰다'.

examples.ko: 할머니 집 변소는 마당 끝에 있었어요.
examples.en: The outhouse at my grandmother's house was at the end of the yard.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 밤에 변소 가는 게 무서웠어요.
examples.en: As a child, I was scared of going to the toilet at night.

examples.ko: 옛날 학교에는 변소가 건물 밖에 있었어요.
examples.en: In old schools, the toilet was outside the building.

examples.ko: 변소에서 나는 냄새 때문에 창문을 열었어요.
examples.en: I opened the window because of the smell from the toilet.

examples.ko: 이야기 속 주인공은 변소 쪽으로 몰래 걸어갔어요.
examples.en: In the story, the main character quietly walked toward the toilet.
These days people say restroom instead of outhouse.

explain: '화장실'보다 낡고 거친 느낌이라서 요즘 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 써요. 옛날 이야기나 재래식 화장실을 말할 때 들려요. '뒷간'도 비슷한 옛말이에요.

phrases.example: 어릴 때는 밤에 혼자 변소에 가기가 무서웠어요.
phrases.en: As a child, I was scared to go to the outhouse alone at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 옛날 이야기에서 화장실에 간다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in old-time stories to say someone goes to the toilet.

phrases.en: In the old days, the outhouse was outside the house.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변소'와 비슷한 옛말이에요. 요즘은 거의 안 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: An old word similar to 변소. Rarely used nowadays.

phrases.en: Where is the restroom?
phrases.nuance_ko: 요즘 일상에서 쓰는 보통 말이에요. 말할 때는 '변소' 대신 이 말을 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ordinary word used today. Use this instead of 변소 when speaking.

explain_en: It sounds older and cruder than '화장실', so it is rarely used in everyday conversation today. You hear it in old stories or when talking about old-style toilets. '뒷간' is a similar old word.
